items.origin_mathematical_context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
items.title: Ordinary category without imposed smallness
items.draft_definition: A (possibly large) category C consists of collections Ob(C) of objects and Mor(C) of morphisms, source and target assignments s,t:Mor(C)→Ob(C), an identity 1_X:X→X for every object X, and a composition g∘f:X→Z for each composable pair f:X→Y and g:Y→Z. Composition is associative and the identities are two-sided units. These collections and operations must be interpreted in a fixed foundation or universe framework; neither Ob(C) nor Mor(C) is required here to be a set.
conditions: Specify a workable foundational interpretation for classes/collections and arrows; class-size language does not itself imply a particular universe scheme.
Do not assume smallness or locally small Hom sets unless a particular provider requires it.
edge_cases: The empty category satisfies the axioms: no objects, no arrows, and identity axioms vacuous.
A small category is a size-restricted specialization, not an identical meaning.
Locally small means each Hom_C(X,Y) is a set; this is not part of the unrestricted base definition.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: Smallness imposes a set of objects (and corresponding size convention), which the generic candidate does not.

source_checks_required: Provider-specific foundational assumptions (small/local-small/large) and exact available primary locator.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Category theory: ordinary functor between arbitrary categories C and D without assuming smallness; object/arrow assignments preserve identities and compositions.
items.title: Ordinary covariant functor between arbitrary categories
items.draft_definition: Given categories C and D in a fixed common foundational framework, a covariant functor F:C→D assigns an object F(X) of D to each object X of C and a morphism F(f):F(X)→F(Y) of D to every morphism f:X→Y in C, such that F(1_X)=1_{F(X)} for every X and F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f) for every composable pair f,g.
conditions: The object/arrow assignments must be legitimate collections or class maps in the chosen foundation.
Neither C nor D is assumed small.
edge_cases: The unique functor from the empty category to any category exists; a functor from a nonempty category to the empty category does not.
Contravariant functors reverse arrow direction, or equivalently are covariant C^op→D, and require a separate variant.
Fully faithful or representable functors have additional conditions and are not synonymous with ordinary functors.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: The populated definition has small-category hypotheses; this draft preserves arbitrary categories.

source_checks_required: Verify whether the chosen source permits large categories and whether it requires locally small Hom sets.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
items.title: Quotient of a commutative unital ring by an ideal
items.draft_definition: Let A be a commutative ring with identity and I an ideal of A. The quotient ring A/I has the additive cosets a+I as elements and operations (a+I)+(b+I)=(a+b)+I and (a+I)(b+I)=ab+I; its identity is 1_A+I. The canonical map π:A→A/I, a↦a+I, is a surjective unital ring homomorphism with kernel I.
conditions: I is an ideal, not necessarily prime, maximal or proper.
The zero ring is allowed unless the selected source explicitly excludes it.
edge_cases: I=A gives A/I the zero ring, with 0=1; I=0 gives an isomorphic copy of A.
A/I is an integral domain exactly when I is prime (using the proper-ideal convention), and a field exactly when I is maximal.
The quotient by a non-two-sided ideal in a noncommutative ring need not be a ring; this draft is commutative.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: The total quotient ring is a localization at regular elements; A/I is a coset quotient.

source_checks_required: Check zero-ring policy and source convention for unital homomorphisms.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
items.title: Set-theoretic preimage or inverse image
items.draft_definition: Let f:X→Y be a function and B⊆Y. The inverse image (preimage) of B under f is f^{-1}[B]:={x∈X | f(x)∈B}. This construction is defined for every function f; no inverse function or injectivity/surjectivity is required.
conditions: B is a subset of the codomain Y; f is an ordinary function.
edge_cases: f^{-1}[∅]=∅ and f^{-1}[Y]=X, including when X=∅.
Inverse images preserve unions, intersections and relative complements.
For continuous f the preimage of an open subset is open; continuity is an additional condition, not part of this set-theoretic construction.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: A function inverse requires bijectivity and differs from its action on subsets; prime-ideal contraction is a typed use of preimage.

source_checks_required: Identify a source with general set-theoretic preimage notation and optional topological/application variants.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
items.title: Polynomial ring on a set of commuting indeterminates
items.draft_definition: Let R be a commutative unital ring and I a set. The polynomial ring R[X_i:i∈I] consists of finitely supported functions a:ℕ^{(I)}→R, where ℕ^{(I)} denotes finitely supported exponent vectors on I. Write a as the formal finite sum Σ_α a_α X^α. Addition is coefficientwise and multiplication uses convolution (ab)_γ=Σ_{α+β=γ}a_α b_β. The constant polynomial 1_R is the identity, and the indeterminates commute with one another and R.
conditions: I is a set of indeterminates; each individual polynomial has finite support, even if I is infinite.
R is commutative with 1; a noncommutative free algebra requires a distinct variant.
edge_cases: I=∅ gives R canonically; R=0 yields the zero polynomial ring.
No evaluation or chosen root of a polynomial is implied by this formal construction.
A power series ring replaces finite monomial support by an appropriately defined infinite-series model, not the same meaning.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: Individual polynomial-based constructions do not define the general polynomial ring.

source_checks_required: Check exact notation and arbitrary-index-set formulation in a credible algebra reference; verify zero ring and source-specific coefficient conventions.

items.origin_candidate_query: residue field of a local ring
items.origin_mathematical_context: Commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: residue field A/m of a commutative local ring (A,m), including the prime-localized κ(p)=R_p/pR_p and the scheme-point κ(s)=O_{S,s}/m_s.
items.title: Residue field of a local ring or at a prime
items.draft_definition: For a commutative local ring (A,m), where m is its unique maximal ideal, the residue field is κ(A):=A/m. More generally, for a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R, the residue field at p is κ(p):=R_p/pR_p, the quotient of the local ring R_p by its maximal ideal. For a point x of a locally ringed space, its residue field is O_{X,x}/m_x.
conditions: A local ring has a proper maximal ideal; the zero ring does not have a maximal ideal under the proper-ideal convention.
The point-stalk application presupposes the local ringed-space structure.
edge_cases: R_p/pR_p is a field whether or not p is maximal in R.
For p maximal in R, κ(p) is canonically isomorphic to R/p.
Distinguish quotient residue fields from fraction fields, even when both occur in examples.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: The residue field is a particular maximal-ideal quotient, not a synonym for either the ambient local ring or an abstract field.

source_checks_required: Check κ(x), κ(p) and A/m source variants and actual source convention for localization.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Commutative algebra: associative commutative ring R with a specified multiplicative identity 1_R; the prime-ideal formulation does not assume the ring is an integral domain.
items.title: Commutative associative ring with identity
items.draft_definition: A commutative unital ring R is a set equipped with addition +, multiplication ·, and elements 0_R,1_R such that (R,+,0_R) is an abelian group, multiplication is associative and commutative, 1_R·a=a for every a∈R, and multiplication distributes over addition on both sides.
conditions: The structure includes a multiplicative identity; unless stated otherwise, 1_R need not differ from 0_R.
An integral-domain specialization additionally requires nonzero ring and the absence of zero divisors.
edge_cases: If 1_R=0_R, then a=a·1_R=a·0_R=0_R for all a; the zero ring is the sole such ring.
A bare ring may be interpreted nonunital or noncommutative by other sources; never silently identify those conventions.
Ring homomorphism identity-preservation is a separate convention and should be explicit.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: Integral domains require nonzero and no zero divisors; arbitrary commutative unital rings do not.

source_checks_required: Choose and cite a provider's ring convention; specify zero-ring allowance.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Module theory: free left R-module over a unital ring with an R-basis, equivalently a direct sum R^{(I)} of copies of R, possibly infinite rank.
items.title: Free left module of arbitrary rank
items.draft_definition: Let R be an associative ring with identity. A left R-module F is free if there exist a set I and elements (e_i)_{i∈I} such that every x∈F admits a unique expression x=Σ_{i∈I} r_i e_i with coefficients r_i∈R, only finitely many nonzero. Equivalently, F≅⊕_{i∈I} R as left R-modules; (e_i) is a basis indexed by I.
conditions: The scalar action is unital: 1_R x=x.
I may be any set, finite, infinite, or empty; R need not be commutative.
edge_cases: The empty basis gives the zero module.
For the zero ring, the zero module may admit bases indexed by distinct sets; basis cardinality is not a well-defined invariant in full generality.
An arbitrary associative unital noncommutative ring may fail invariant basis number; do not assume rank uniqueness without a suitable hypothesis.
Free does not mean finite free, projective-only, or merely locally free.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: Finite locally free modules need not be globally free, and arbitrary free modules can have infinite bases.

source_checks_required: Source exact rank/basis and left/right convention; check treatment of zero ring and invariant basis number.

items.origin_mathematical_context: Module theory: quotient left R-module M/N by an R-submodule N, whose elements are additive cosets m+N with addition and R-scalar action induced by M. Includes ideal modules I/I², successive filtration quotient modules and regular-module quotients R/I; extra ring, graded, flatness, or field structure is not part of this quotient-module meaning.
items.title: Quotient left module by a submodule
items.draft_definition: Let R be a ring, M a left R-module, and N≤M an R-submodule. The quotient module M/N consists of additive cosets m+N with operations (m+N)+(m'+N)=(m+m')+N and r(m+N)=rm+N for r∈R. The canonical map M→M/N is surjective and R-linear with kernel N.
conditions: For the standard unital-module convention, R has 1 and 1·m=m; the quotient construction also exists for coherent nonunital-action conventions.
N is a submodule, so the induced operations are well defined.
edge_cases: N=M gives the zero module; N=0 recovers a canonical copy of M.
For M=R as a left module and N a left ideal, R/N is an R-module; a ring multiplication on R/N additionally requires N to be two-sided.
Subquotients I/I² are instances, but do not identify the quotient-module construction with specific ideal, filtration or graded structures.

accepted_independent_comparisons.explanation: Quotient rings, quotient modules and more specialized filtration quotients differ in underlying structures and extra operations.

source_checks_required: Verify source left/right and unital conventions; distinguish submodule quotient from ideal quotient in each parent.
